bearings.paper_claim: Eq. 6 HAC is a weighted sum of lagged products of estimating functions. Investment example RealGNP SE is 0.0168 (Newey-West lag 4, no prewhitening), 0.0236 (Newey-West automatic bandwidth with prewhitening) and 0.0208 (Parzen kernel, VAR(2) prewhitening, no finite-sample adjustment). Spread about 40 percent (0.0236 vs 0.0168). Coefficient 0.1691 is significant under all three; paper says the estimators give slightly different SEs but agree on the conclusion.
bearings.system_side: SEATS-W hand-codes a Bartlett Newey-West SE at fixed lags 2, 4 and 8 weeks, lag pairs matched within cycle by calendar week, n/(n-k) adjustment, no prewhitening and no automatic bandwidth, labelled secondary with no p-value. Primary inference is a fixed-X moving-block bootstrap with Holm.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Paper examples are time series; RealInt has 103 quarterly obs (1961(1)-1986(3)); Investment length is not stated in the text (fitted series starts 1964). The text does not call the series stationary and gives no coverage evidence at weekly-panel sizes. The ~40 percent spread supports showing several lag settings, not validating any one lag.
bearings.verifier_note: Numbers, eq. 6, lag choices and code lines check out. Softened because the rel's 'stationary macro series of about 40-100 observations' is not supported by the paper text.

bearings.paper_claim: On the public schools data (51 states, Wisconsin NA dropped, N=50), the quadratic income term has SE 830, z 1.91, p 0.056 under HC0 and SE 5489, z 0.29, p 0.77 under HC4. Paper attributes the gap to one high-leverage outlier (Alaska) and HC4's leverage correction. It cites Long and Ervin (2000) for HC3 as best in small samples and makes HC3 the vcovHC default.
bearings.paper_location: Sec 3.1 p.5; Sec 4.1 p.10-11 and Figure 2
bearings.system_side: Refit robustness block prints an HC1 row via sandwich::vcovHC type HC1, beside CR1, CR2 (clubSandwich) and a wild cluster restricted bootstrap. Fixture row: HC1 SE 0.0395 on 11 df for the pac G_current model.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper's HC0 vs HC4 contrast is an estimator-choice comparison on one 50-state cross-section with one outlier. It does not show HC1 understates SEs in the refit's ~11 df regressions. The HC1 understatement point is the analyst's inference from cited small-sample literature, not a result in this paper. The paper has no simulation.
bearings.verifier_note: Numbers and code lines confirmed. Softened: 'leverage drives HC choice' and 'one leverage point moving p from .056 to .77' blend an estimator change (HC0 to HC4) with a single outlier, and the HC1 understatement claim is not in the paper.

bearings.paper_claim: HC variants use the sandwich form (X'X)^-1 X' Omega X (X'X)^-1 with diagonal Omega weights built from residuals and the hat-matrix diagonal; HC0 to HC4 differ only in these weights.
bearings.system_side: sgs_estimate.R hand-codes an HC1 sandwich V = (n/df) A X'uu'X A, labelled reference only. DESCRIPTIVE tests report the estimate and the HC1 error only; inference is a wild cluster restricted bootstrap with Webb weights. The Holm step was not seen in this file.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Context only. Any HC3 column for DESCRIPTIVE fits is an UNVERIFIED suggestion until a second path reproduces it (DE-062).
bearings.verifier_note: Paper equations and the code line match. The rel's Holm detail was not confirmed in sgs_estimate.R, so it is flagged rather than asserted.

related.why: The paper points to Zeileis 2006b, Object-Oriented Computation of Sandwich Estimators, as the follow-up implementation. The rel's claim that it generalizes to any model with estimating functions and bread was not confirmed in this paper's text, so the link rests on the paper's own citation.

Later work by Zeileis, Koll and Graham on clustered covariances in the same sandwich package. This 2004 paper does not cite it, so the link is real but is not a citation from this paper. The vcovCL use in the Mentat refit is a code fact, not something this paper supports.

summary_issues: summary_md says the paper's examples support the SEATS-W fixed-lag design. The paper shows lag and prewhitening sensitivity only; it does not endorse fixed lags 2, 4 and 8.
summary_md says Mentat robust rows use HC1 throughout. Only the refit robustness block and sgs_estimate.R were checked; no full census was run.
summary_md says the package versions match registry/models.json. The paper does state sandwich 3.1-3, lmtest 0.9-40, strucchange 1.5-4 and zoo 1.9-0 (p.18), but the registry file was not opened.
rel bearing 2 code_ref rf_robust.R:8 should be :9 (the vcovHC line); line 8 is the rf_hc1 function header.
rel bearing 1 transfer_conditions describes the examples as stationary macro series of about 40-100 observations; the paper states neither the stationarity nor the Investment series length.
rel bearing 2 says a single leverage point moves p from .056 to .77; that contrast is an HC0 vs HC4 estimator change, and the paper attributes it to one outlier plus the HC4 correction.
rel related 'various-versatile-variances' is real (title and abstract confirm clustered covariances in sandwich) but postdates and is not cited by this 2004 paper.
